## Shared scientific figure contract and mathematical agent algorithm — 2026-10-13

For evidence-grounded scientific figures, physics-driven diagrams, animations, research-agent figure handoffs, or editable engineering slides, apply `project/SCIENTIFIC_DESIGN_RESEARCH_AGENT_ALGORITHMS_V1.md`. The contract example is `scripts/figure_contract_example.json`; run `python scripts/validate_figure_contract.py scripts/figure_contract_example.json` and `python -m unittest discover -s scripts -p 'test_figure_contract.py' -v` as *structural* admission tests. The validator does NOT verify physics, external citations, measurement authenticity, model fidelity, actual PowerPoint playback or independent scientific release gates. Preserve the thermal-only scope, current source-of-truth title and objectives, frozen eight-slide three-minute master, separate ten-slide training variant, evidence rule and exact Deck3 color/typography policies. This routing supplements existing instructions; do not promote I2/I3 candidates or treat A0–A8 roles as deployed autonomous agents.

# Scientific Engineering Animation AI Skill V1

**Status:** Supplemental production procedure, NOT scientific evidence or a new active-thesis scope. Existing thesis authorities, frozen objectives, 13-color Deck3 palette, approved presentation variants and source/rights standards control all outputs.

## 0. Resolve authority and presentation variant

Read `AI_RESEARCH_INSTRUCTIONS.md`, `project/CURRENT_THESIS_AUTHORITY_INDEX_V1.md`, `project/CANONICAL_EVIDENCE_NON_INVENTION_STANDARD_V1.md`, the current thermal scope and state-time authorities, and `.github/skills/deck3/references/DECK3_SCIENTIFIC_MINIMAL_INFOGRAPHIC_STANDARD_V1.md`. For Deck3 tasks, read `thesis/presentations/deck3/DECK3_PRESENTATION_MASTER_ROUTER_V1.md` first.

**Variant routing:** The canonical **three-minute, eight-slide** Deck3 remains frozen. The user's **ten-slide training presentation (Title / Outline / six core content areas / Remaining Work / Thank You)** is a separate educational/visualization variant; do not overwrite or renumber eight-slide or 13/14-slide approved masters. Preserve user-approved copy and objective wording as-is.

## 1. Mandatory figure contract — before drawing

For each animation record:
1. Figure ID, presentation variant, slide title, **one scientific message**, audience and desired camera/viewport.
2. Physical boundaries, precise component IDs, ports, topology, source/target and units (when relevant).
3. Arrow ledger with ID, origin, destination, semantic type, evidence/provenance, conditional sign and required visual treatment.
4. Whether each visible quantity is external forcing, internal state, algebraic electrical quantity, capability, service, control, observation, experimental measurement or mathematical model output.
5. Distinct **narrative reveal time** versus **physical model time**. If time is narrative, label it as presentation sequence only; animation seconds may not be passed off as thermal constants, control delays, power propagation or physical recovery time.
6. Original artwork/source rights, actual equipment qualification, unresolved evidence, target formats and editable layer plan.

Minimum review question: Would motion or style make a hypothetical I2/I3 pathway look observed? If yes, stop/redesign.

## 2. Controlled arrow and motion semantics

Use the existing seven-arrow ontology: **A** AC electrical energy/power transfer; **B** thermal energy transfer; **C** control/intervention; **D** observation/measurement; **E** proposed directional functional/causal hypothesis; **F** methodological sequence; **G** external exposure/forcing.

- Ordinary normal charging: **P1 transformer → P2 AC radial feeder → T1 charger (AC/DC conversion) → T2 vehicle battery**. Power System and Electrified Transportation are separate system boundaries; the AC grid-side port belongs at the charger input.
- Transformer cooling **P4** belongs to P1; charger cooling **T3** belongs within T1; transformer control/protection **P3** must be an independently qualified signal path; vehicle HVAC **T4** is a vehicle auxiliary load, not an independent feeder connection.
- Revealing the arrows successively (e.g., six seconds) is explanatory motion, NOT simulated charge flow velocity.
- Common high ambient temperature is external forcing applied separately to equipment, not cross-infrastructure thermal causality. No universal bidirectional power flow, EVSE derating law, battery thermal limit, transformer trip/charger curtailment or reverse export without verified configuration.
- **I2/H1 candidate T_e→P:** charger thermal/cooling state → actual grid-side AC P/Q demand **only if verified** → grid loading → transformer thermal state, with feedback assumptions and alternatives documented.
- **I3/H2 candidate P→T_e:** transformer thermal condition → documented sensing/actuation → actual charging permission/power effect **only if qualified**.
- Candidate E edges must stay visually identified as **proposed / not yet qualified** in EVERY visible frame where their causal reading is possible.

## 3. Production pipeline (vector first)

**Design science and storyboard → vector geometry → optional numerical state source → animation sequence → encoding → editable PPTX companion → G0–G7 audit.**

1. Load `scientific-diagram-design` for diagram grammar and semantic boundaries; `scientific-infographic-design` for hierarchy and sources; `mathematical-visualization-design` for model-derived geometry/time; and `deck3` for PPTX assembly and governance.
2. Draw original equipment symbols/components using SVG or native vector objects; do not reproduce copyrighted figure arrangements or fake ASU marks. Layer IDs include boundaries, equipment, ports, arrows, separate labels and provenance.
3. For physical-time animation, numerically compute `x(t)` with explicit governing law, provenance, initial conditions, parameters, integration tolerances, units, uncertainty and validation status. If absent, use **static diagram or illustrative reveal**, never create fabricated trajectories.
4. Choose only necessary motion: staged reveal for architecture or narrative; continuous motion only for explicitly modeled/observed processes; highlight transitions or interactions only when physically justified. State in output whether time is model-time or presenter-time.
5. Encode with SVG + CairoSVG/FFmpeg for vector-first media; use Manim/SciPy for genuine equation/state animation as necessary; GSAP for web/SVG interaction; 3D tools only where depth explains a physical or geometric fact.
6. Build a **separate** native editable PPTX: Times New Roman text, lines, arrows, labels, equations, legends, citations and boundary shapes. Embedded GIF/MP4 objects do not make their internal labels editable; do not conflate an MP4 with native on-click object-level animations.
7. Inspect original/source, beginning/middle/end frames, key state/threshold times if modeled, exported dimensions, readability, collisions, color tokens, fonts, motion semantics and any rendered PPTX. **Actual Microsoft PowerPoint slideshow replay remains NOT_RUN until tested there**; XML or PDF render checks do not substitute.

## 4. Non-negotiable design system

Use exact authored palette: `#FFFFFF #000000 #12304A #0072B2 #416985 #006D70 #087E98 #176B42 #B4232C #555D66 #8C1D40 #FFC627 #6ACEEE`. Pure white canvas and all panels, no gradients or decorative colored fills/shadows. Gold reserved for authorized institutional accent; natural vegetation/context and authentic equipment photo materials may retain realistic natural colors without changing authored scientific marks. Use Times New Roman for slide/native text, labels and animation typography where available. Default 16:9, PPTX **13.333333 × 7.5 in**, 1920×1080 poster target; keep scientific text legible when projected.

## 5. Outputs and release gate

Produce (where relevant) `figure.svg`, `animation.mp4`, `animation.gif`, `figure_editable.pptx`, original source code, deterministic manifest, source rights/evidence/edge ledger, and QA record. Record hashes, dimensions, frame rate, duration, tool versions and physical-time status. Use the companion `references/ANIMATION_QA_CHECKLIST_V1.md`; G0–G7 are **non-compensatory**. FAIL/OPEN/NOT_RUN is mandatory when evidence or test unavailable. Do not declare animation scientifically validated simply because rendering passed.

See `examples/CHARGING_PATHWAY_STORYBOARD_V1.md` for an original four-component sequential-reveal test.
